head: FourTrack: a four-track cassette recorder app for iPhone, iPad and Mac
dek: FourTrack lets you record a song in four layers like an old tape machine: play one part, then record the next on top of it. It came out on 13 November for $5.99 and was #87 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 16 November.
details: Each of the four channels has volume, pan, mute, solo, a three-band EQ and one effect (reverb, echo or chorus). A tape setting adds saturation, wow, flutter and hiss, with two tape speeds, plus compression and a limiter. Every take is kept, so recording over a part doesn't lose the old one. Mixes save as WAV or AAC; the listing says there's no account, no ads and no tracking, and recordings stay on the device. It's made by Milo Devereux and needs iOS 17 or later.
where: iPhone, iPad and Mac, $5.99, out since 13 November
means: If you write songs or want to sketch ideas with a tape sound, this is a one-time purchase that records and mixes four tracks on your phone.
todo: The listing recommends wired or USB headphones while recording over earlier parts, because Bluetooth adds a delay.
